what_is_allowed: Nothing. Internet diagnosis and treatment prescriptions must be issued by the treating physician personally; AI auto-generating prescriptions is strictly prohibited, and AI software may not substitute for the physician.
drug_scope: All prescriptions issued in internet diagnosis/treatment
start_date: 2022-02-08 (signed; posted on NHC site 2022-03-15; publicised June 2022)
legal_basis: Internet Diagnosis and Treatment Supervision Rules (Trial) (互联网诊疗监管细则（试行）), NHC General Office + NATCM Office, 国卫办医发〔2022〕2号, art. 13 and art. 21
notes: Verified 2026-11-12 in the NHC Gazette (国家卫生健康委员会公报 2022 No.1, pp. 31-33) hosted on nhc.gov.cn (other_urls[0]); the NHC notice page itself still returns HTTP 412 to scripts, a saved copy of it is other_urls[1]. Art. 13: '其他人员、人工智能软件等不得冒用、替代医师本人提供诊疗服务'. Art. 21: '处方应由接诊医师本人开具，严禁使用人工智能等自动生成处方'. Earlier record had source_date 2022-06-09 (press date) and doc number missing. Arguably also restricts AI-drafted prescriptions (rung 1).

what_is_allowed: Nothing. Internet hospitals must route e-prescriptions through the provincial medical-insurance e-prescription centre and may not use AI to auto-generate prescriptions.
drug_scope: Prescriptions dispensed through medical-insurance designated retail pharmacies
legal_basis: Hunan Healthcare Security Administration, 关于进一步加强基本医疗保障定点零售药店管理的通知 (湘医保发〔2025〕8号), section 二(五)
notes: Notice text opened on the Hunan HSA site 2026-11-12: internet hospitals '须按规定接入省医保电子处方中心并进行电子处方流转，处方行为须严格执行…《互联网诊疗监管细则（试行）》…等有关规定，应与患者或患者家属进行有效、充分的沟通问诊，严禁使用人工智能等自动生成处方。' Restates the 2022 national art. 21 for medical-insurance e-prescriptions. Earlier record cited only a newspaper page.

what_is_allowed: Nothing. Online prescription-drug retail platforms may not use AI to review, approve or renew prescriptions; pharmacist review cannot be delegated to AI; platforms must block AI-generated or fake prescriptions.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensed pharmacists for review; prescriber unchanged
start_date: 2026-05-25 (released 'Monday' per Sixth Tone 2026-05-27; after Sept 2025 draft)
legal_basis: NMPA Compliance Guidelines for Online Retail of Prescription Drugs
notes: NMPA text still not located: nmpa.gov.cn returns HTTP 412 to scripts and renders blank in a browser; gov.cn policy library has no copy (only SAMR Order 58, 2022). Wording differs between the two press sources: Sixth Tone says platforms 'cannot use AI to review, approve, or renew prescriptions'; Caixin says reviews 'must be conducted by licensed pharmacists and cannot be delegated to other personnel or artificial intelligence' and platforms 'must use technology to identify and block AI-generated and fake prescriptions', and does not mention renewal. The rung-2 'renew' reading rests on Sixth Tone alone until the NMPA text is opened.

what_is_allowed: AI may support a doctor only within the doctor's scope; 'AI is not a substitute for your clinical judgement, and you remain responsible for all your clinical decisions and actions.' Doctors 'must not use AI to impersonate yourself in medical practice, including through avatars or chatbots'; registration and practising certificate 'cannot be transferred to an AI system'. Patients must be told explicitly about high-risk AI that influences clinical decisions; informed consent needed where AI plays a significant role in treatment.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Registered doctor. Separately, Council's prescribing statement says the doctor who signs a repeat prescription takes responsibility for it, and Medicines Regulations 1984 reg. 39 bars prescribing except for a patient under the doctor's care.
legal_basis: Medical Council of New Zealand, Guidance on using artificial intelligence (AI) in patient care (March 2026), paras 4, 6, 7, 9; Statement on good prescribing practice (Feb 2024) paras 2, 34-35
notes: Soft-law guidance against rungs 2-4; nearest NZ analogue to Singapore AIHGle. Not prescription-specific, but para 6 (registration cannot transfer to AI) is the clearest regulator line in the region that an AI cannot be the practitioner. Prescribing statement para 35: patients needing assessment 'should not receive repeat prescriptions without being seen by a doctor'. Near-neighbour: a Director-General waiver lets NZePS 'Signature Exempt Prescriptions' be issued electronically without the prescriber's personal signature (still prescriber-issued).

what_is_allowed: Prescribing without a real-time direct consultation (in person, video or phone) 'is not good practice and is not supported by the Board', including asynchronous requests by text, email, live-chat or online 'based on the patient completing a health questionnaire, when the practitioner has never spoken with the patient.' Exception: a patient's usual practitioner may in certain circumstances prescribe without a consultation. Does not mention AI.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Medical practitioner, who 'must be able to explain how the prescribing and the management of the patient was appropriate and necessary.'
expiry: Review at least every five years
legal_basis: Medical Board of Australia, Guidelines: Telehealth consultations with patients (2023), under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law
notes: Near-neighbour restriction: a questionnaire-only renewal model (the Utah Doctronic pattern) would breach this guideline even with a human signer who never spoke to the patient, unless that signer is the patient's usual practitioner. Effective date taken from 'Page reviewed 1/09/2023'; PDF not opened.

what_is_allowed: Practitioners may use AI, but 'Regardless of what technology is used in providing healthcare the practitioner remains responsible' and 'Practitioners must apply human judgment to any output of AI.' TGA approval of a tool does not remove the practitioner's duty of human oversight.
legal_basis: Ahpra / National Boards, Meeting your professional obligations when using Artificial Intelligence in healthcare
notes: Like the Japan MHLW notice, loosely meets the rung-1 inclusion test: does not mention prescribing; case studies cover scribes and dictation only. Date is the 'Page reviewed' stamp.
